_comment: Categories that will ship BELOW the 5-creator target because the search is finished and this is what exists. Only add an entry once you have actually stopped looking for that specific category — a domain having had one pass proves nothing. Each reason says what was searched and what was found, to the same standard as critic-gaps.json. The 5-minimum is a target the owner knowingly traded away rather than loosen the scope rule; this file is where that trade is made visible. Empty is correct until a category's search is genuinely done.

addiction-recovery.reason: Searched deliberately rather than opportunistically: 13 candidate handles probed, 5 resolved. Included: Addiction Policy Forum (non-profit, interviews named researchers, nothing sold) and Sober Powered (a coach, explicitly not a clinician, whose post-acute withdrawal material is hard to find elsewhere). @NIDAnews is an unrelated Arabic-language news channel; @AlcoholMastery has one upload.
addiction-recovery.challenged: The owner challenged the original exclusion of @TheRecoveryVillage, correctly: it was excluded on conflict of interest alone, which is a stricter standard than this project applies anywhere else — commercial interest is normally disclosed with sells-course or sponsor-heavy and left to the visitor to weigh. Re-examined on content instead. Its long-form output is patient testimonials and staff Q&As, its mid-length band is more testimonials plus admissions and insurance explainers ('Understanding Your Admission Process', '7 Myths Around Using Insurance for Rehab'), and the remainder is generic meditation and nutrition filler unrelated to addiction. It does carry genuinely useful withdrawal-timeline and detox-danger explainers, but those are ~3-minute clips. The deciding test: would this be included if a non-profit ran it? No — the substantive content is too thin and too marketing-shaped, the same standard that excluded GitKraken, Zapier and Big Interview. @AllenCarrsEasyway fails identically: 4 long-form videos, all testimonials. So the exclusions stand, but on content quality rather than on conflict, and the original reasoning was wrong. The commercial-conflict signal was added as a result, so that future cases are disclosed rather than silently dropped.
addiction-recovery.attribution: MIXED, and mostly our criteria rather than absent supply. Supply exists — this is a large, active field on YouTube — but almost all of it is either treatment-provider marketing or unstructured personal testimony. What is genuinely scarce is independent, credentialed, educational content. Under a looser content standard the count would still be 2, because the rejected candidates fail on substance rather than on the rule-12 conflict test; under a looser CREDENTIAL standard it could be higher, since there are many recovery-testimony channels deliberately not pursued.

subAreas: credentialed addiction clinicians and professional bodies
probed: credentialed addiction clinicians and professional bodies
rule18.whatWasTried: The unprobed end at the time of writing was credentialed clinicians rather than providers or testimony. @AddictionMedicine is the American Society of Addiction Medicine: 49 uploads, archived since February 2021, long-form is conference plenaries addressed to physicians rather than to anyone in recovery. @DrKAddiction, @DrAdiJaffe, @gabormate, @recoveryelevator and @sobrietyengine do not resolve; @Dr_Gabor_Mate resolves to a Czech channel with one upload.

first-aid.corrected: THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG AND IS REWRITTEN. It originally read gapCause: absent-supply on the strength of thirteen probes, ALL of which were institutions — Red Cross, NHS, St John Ambulance, ProTrainings, First Aid For Free. The individual-clinician end of the field was never searched. Under rule 18 it was searched, and PrepMedic is there: a critical-care flight paramedic, 353 uploads, 44 long-form videos matching bystander first-aid terms, including a 33-minute explanation of life-saving medications aimed explicitly at bystanders. This is the same failure as the marketing note — a finding from one end of a domain applied to an end never searched — caught twice in two batches by the same rule.
first-aid.reason: What survives, narrowed to what was actually evidenced: THE CERTIFYING BODIES DO NOT TEACH ON VIDEO. British Red Cross has 502 uploads at a one-minute median and its only long-form is about listening and social division; American Red Cross (@redcross, 2,180 uploads) publishes blood-donation interviews; the NHS has one long-form video, a BSL winter leaflet; @sja has 5 uploads, @ProTrainings 5, @firstaidforfree 20. That claim is true and remains on the record. The claim that no usable supply exists was an unwarranted generalisation from it.
first-aid.attribution: MIXED. Genuinely absent: a structured video syllabus from a body qualified to certify, and the reason is defensible rather than negligent — certification requires hands-on assessment, so the course is the product and video is its marketing. Genuinely our criteria: individual credentialed clinicians do publish usable bystander education, and one is now listed. countUnderLooserStandard is 2 rather than a larger number because SkinnyMedic (500k-1M, 1,409 uploads) is the next candidate and fails on content — 36 of 50 recent uploads under two minutes, long-form that is a course promo plus gear, and a catalogue mixing trauma care with firearm reviews. Uncredentialed first-aid presenters were not enumerated and are not counted: under rule 12's acute-recall rationale they are the specific thing not to ship.
first-aid.challenged: Confirmed as a rule 12 category by the owner in batch 19, with a rationale the owner was explicit should stay narrow: not that bad advice is costly over time, but that the content is recalled under acute stress by someone who has no capacity to evaluate it in the moment. The owner also predicted this would end as a documented gap and said that outcome is correct — an empty first-aid category beats a well-produced one from someone unqualified. Re-tested under rule 18 in batch 24 after the owner asked for every absent-supply gap to be re-examined, and it did not survive. The category is no longer empty.

rule18.whatWasTried: All thirteen original probes were institutions. Searching the individual-clinician end found PrepMedic (critical-care flight paramedic, 353 uploads, 44 long-form bystander-first-aid hits) immediately, and SkinnyMedic as a second candidate that fails on content. The gap as written did not survive; the narrower institutional claim did.

conversion-optimization.reason: Nothing in this category is a teaching catalogue. The consultancies are absent or empty (@speero 0 uploads, @Widerfunnel 2, @jeffreyeisenberg 0, @conversionrateexperts 0); the individual practitioners do not resolve (@conversionxl, @GoodUIorg, @behaveio, @richardshotton, @rorysutherland); and @cxl is a handle trap resolving to an unrelated Arabic-language channel with 4,529 uploads.
conversion-optimization.attribution: ABSENT SUPPLY. The two tool vendors with catalogues are thin and product-shaped: Optimizely has 106 uploads with two long-form videos, one an 88-minute conference keynote; AB Tasty has 97 with four, all webinars. Neither teaches the discipline. countUnderLooserStandard is 0 because the looser standard here would mean listing a testing-tool vendor's webinar under a category about research and testing method, which is the vendor-content problem rather than a solution to it.

rule18.whatWasTried: Written only after the marketing and first-aid corrections, so all four sub-areas were probed before the claim was made rather than after. The behavioural-science end does exist — Nudgestock, Ogilvy's behavioural science festival, has 239 uploads with 20 of 49 over twenty minutes and speakers including Charles Spence and Roger Martin. It is NOT mapped here: behaviour change and creativity are adjacent to conversion optimisation, not the same subject, and mapping it would be the credentialed halo effect in a new dress. Recorded as a near-miss rather than used.

conversion-optimization.visitorNote: We looked and did not list anyone. The consultancies have either no channel or an empty one, the practitioners we searched for do not publish on video, and the two testing-tool vendors with real catalogues publish webinars about their own products rather than teaching the discipline.

hiring-and-recruiting.reason: Probed by topic search for long-form video on hiring, interviewing candidates and recruiting process. What came back was the industry selling to itself: 4 Corner Resources is a staffing agency, Spark Hire is recruiting software, Outmatch/Harver is an assessment platform. The nearest thing to teaching was general business channels covering hiring as one topic among many.
hiring-and-recruiting.attribution: ABSENT SUPPLY, for a structural reason worth naming: in this subject the person who would teach is paid by the employer, so their video is a sales asset. countUnderLooserStandard is 2 because a looser standard would admit two vendor channels whose material is competent and entirely shaped by what they sell — which is exactly the trade this project refuses.

rule18.whatWasTried: One topic search on the discipline's own vocabulary. THE CLAIM IS NARROW AND SHOULD BE READ THAT WAY: two of five plausible ends were probed. The I-O psychology end and independent hiring managers are unprobed, and this project's record is that an unprobed end is where the finding usually breaks — six times so far.

hiring-and-recruiting.visitorNote: We looked and did not list anyone. The long-form video on hiring is almost entirely made by the people selling hiring services — staffing agencies, recruiting software, assessment vendors — and we would rather leave this empty than hand you a sales asset. Two ends we have not searched yet: academic work on selection, and hiring managers publishing on their own account.

career-change.reason: Probed by topic search for long-form on changing careers, career transitions and switching industries. The results were media and motivation rather than method: TEDx, Forbes, Udacity, Mel Robbins. Work It Daily was evaluated properly and rejected — genuinely substantial, fourteen of forty-nine uploads over twenty minutes, but its centre is job search and LinkedIn profiles, and both job-search categories here are already served.
career-change.attribution: MIXED, and mostly our criteria. Supply exists in volume; almost all of it is encouragement, and the part that is method belongs to job search rather than to deciding what to move toward. The category blurb asks specifically about testing a direction before committing, and nothing found addresses that. countUnderLooserStandard is 3 if inspiration counts as teaching.

subAreas: people who documented their own transition at length
industry-specific "how I moved into X" channels
rule18.whatWasTried: One topic search plus a full evidence pass on the strongest candidate it returned. Two of five ends probed. The last two — people who documented a transition, and industry-specific accounts — are the ones most likely to contain what the blurb actually asks for, and they are unprobed.

career-change.visitorNote: We looked and did not list anyone. There is a great deal of video about changing careers and almost all of it is encouragement; the part that is method turns out to be job-search advice, which is a different skill and is covered elsewhere here. What this page is meant to be about — testing a direction before you commit to it — we could not find taught. Not yet searched: people who documented their own transition at length.

legal-for-founders.reason: Probed by topic search for long-form on startup legal basics, incorporation, equity and vesting. The only substantial catalogue was LegalVision, a law firm's own channel. Everything else was thin: StartHub 89 uploads, an individual lawyer at 23, one handle at 5 below the credible floor.
legal-for-founders.attribution: MIXED. Supply exists but it is nearly all firms marketing to founders, and legal content carries a problem no other category here has to the same degree: it is jurisdiction-bound. A firm publishes for the jurisdiction it sells in, so its material is both an advertisement and correct for only some readers. countUnderLooserStandard is 1 — LegalVision would be listable if a conflict and a jurisdiction caveat were judged sufficient, and rule 16 already exists for the second half of that.

subAreas: bar associations and public legal-education bodies
rule18.whatWasTried: One topic search covering firms and individuals. Two of five ends probed. Accelerator material — Y Combinator is already in this dataset and publishes on incorporation and equity — is unprobed for this category specifically and is the most likely place this gap breaks.

legal-for-founders.visitorNote: We looked and did not list anyone. Nearly all of it is law firms publishing to attract clients, and legal material has a problem the rest of this site does not: it is only correct in one country. A firm's video is both an advertisement and jurisdiction-specific, and we were not willing to hand you that without being able to say it applies where you are.

body-language.reason: Two rounds. The general probe (batch 50) returned The Behavior Panel — four analysts reading famous interrogations — and an NLP persuasion trainer. The research probe (batch 56), aimed at academic nonverbal-behaviour and deception work, returned the same genre again: The Behavior Panel accounted for 20 of 50 results, alongside three more channels of the same shape. No researcher publishing directly was found.
body-language.attribution: MIXED, and the mix is the point. Supply is enormous; almost all of it is case-reading as entertainment, and the evidence base for confident nonverbal inference is weak enough that the confident tone is itself the problem. The only creator this category has ever had, münecat, is a CRITIC of body-language experts — now archived — so listing a case-reading channel would list precisely what the category's own dissenting voice exists to correct. countUnderLooserStandard is 3 if a large, watchable channel counted regardless of whether its claims are supportable.
body-language.visitorNote: We looked twice and did not list anyone. There is a great deal of body-language content and almost all of it is the same thing: confident readings of famous people from video, presented as expertise. The research on inferring intent from nonverbal behaviour does not support that confidence, and we could not find anyone teaching what it does support. The one creator this page ever had was a critic of the genre rather than a teacher of it, and her channel has stopped.

rule18.whatWasTried: Two topic searches, the second aimed specifically at the research end that the first had not reached. Three of five sub-areas probed. The two unprobed ends — interview-training professionals and clinical communication teaching — are where this finding would most plausibly break, and both are places the subject is taught without the mind-reading claim attached.

_schema: Each entry: reason (what was searched and found), gapCause (absent-supply | our-criteria | mixed), countUnderLooserStandard, challenged (any reasoning contested and re-examined), and RULE 18 — rule18: { testedAt, subAreas[], probed[], outcome: survived|falsified, whatWasTried }. An entry without a rule18 block is UNFINISHED, not documented: a gap nobody tried to disprove is indistinguishable from a search that stopped early. probed must cover every sub-area listed, because the failure mode caught twice in this project is a finding from one end of a domain applied to ends never searched. A falsified finding keeps a `corrected` field stating what the entry originally claimed and why that was wrong, rather than being quietly rewritten — see first-aid.

exam-preparation.found: Two rounds. Discovery returned only creators already listed here plus a productivity-business channel and a memory-technique channel belonging to another category; recall added a medical-careers channel and one whose last upload was March 2022.
exam-preparation.smallRound: A --small round aimed at examiners and revision technique returned subject tutors: the strongest, Mr Salles Teaches English, is a working teacher with 1,472 uploads, but the subject is AQA GCSE English rather than exam method, and it is locked to one exam board in one country.
exam-preparation.conclusion: Retirement stands. Three rounds, the last one deliberately below the commercial top.

journaling.found: Two rounds, including the therapeutic-writing end that the first round had not touched. The largest channel in the subject is journaling as craft — planner setups, sticker collections — which is what this category's blurb distinguishes against; the therapeutic end returned trauma-recovery podcasts rather than anyone teaching the practice.
journaling.smallRound: A --small round in the vocabulary of the practice — morning pages, notebook method, writing teacher — returned audio libraries, general lifestyle vlogs and a manuscript institute. No teacher of the practice at any size.
journaling.conclusion: Retirement stands. Three rounds, the last one deliberately below the commercial top.

deep-work-and-focus.found: Two rounds returned ambient study music, motivational channels, a documentary strand, and two creators already listed. The subject has an enormous audience and almost no independent teaching.
deep-work-and-focus.smallRound: A --small round on attention training and sustained concentration returned meditation music, an English-practice channel and a medical college. Nothing on the subject.
deep-work-and-focus.conclusion: Retirement stands. Three rounds, the last one deliberately below the commercial top.

self-discipline.found: Discovery returned Huberman, TEDx, Mel Robbins and a podcast collision — motivation rather than method, which is the shape this subject takes at scale.
self-discipline.smallRound: A --small round in the research vocabulary — implementation intentions, self-control — returned a psychology podcast, reuploaded Jim Rohn seminars, and one creator already listed here.
self-discipline.conclusion: Retirement stands. Three rounds, the last one deliberately below the commercial top.

affiliate-marketing.found: Every candidate returned was a make-money-online channel. The one creator listed already carries a caveat that his current catalogue has moved away from the subject.
unprobed: practitioners who publish operating detail rather than income claims

sleep-quality.found: Two rounds. The strongest candidate, IntraBalance, is a Harvard-trained sleep physician — and states it is built specifically for clinicians, with practice-building content alongside the clinical material, which is the ground Physiotutors was rejected on in batch 43. Insomnia Coach is 47 of 50 uploads under two minutes with client testimonials as its long-form.
unprobed: academic sleep laboratories publishing for the public
CBT-I programmes run by health services

prompt-engineering.found: Two rounds returned certification mills (Simplilearn at 12,403 uploads, edureka at 11,895) and two creators already listed here. The subject's independent teaching appears to happen in writing rather than video.

personal-budgeting.found: Two rounds. The strongest candidate, The Budget Mom, is 30 of 50 uploads under two minutes with a single long case study; the rest of the field is spending vlogs. The incumbent is an institution doing explainers, and what is missing is a practitioner with a catalogue rather than a feed.

dating-skills.found: One round. The field is dominated by coaching channels at extreme volume — one candidate has 10,537 uploads — in the seduction-advice genre. Recorded at one round because nothing found was close enough to warrant a second.
unprobed: clinicians working on social anxiety and dating

breathwork.found: Two rounds. The first returned the Buteyko tradition the listed creator already represents, plus physiology-lecture channels for medical students. The second, aimed at respiratory physiotherapy and clinical breathing work, returned the same medical-lecture channels again — Ninja Nerd, Dr Najeeb, Medicosis — which teach the physiology to students rather than the practice to anyone.
unprobed: clinical anxiety programmes using breathing protocols

bike-maintenance.found: Two rounds for an ACTIVE second voice. The category does have a second listing — RJ The Bike Guy, whose repair archive is strong — but he stopped posting in July 2025, so the page shows one live channel and one archive. The second round returned bike-tech news and product coverage (GCN Tech is 33 of 50 uploads under two minutes) rather than maintenance teaching.
unprobed: bike co-ops and community workshops publishing their teaching
bike-maintenance.note: Distinct from the other entries here: this category is not empty of a second voice, it is empty of a live one.

salary-negotiation.found: Discovery on negotiation scripts and counter-offers returned career-advice generalists, university careers offices and recruiting-agency channels. The two closest were Sonal Bahl, whose long-form is a weekly career AMA rather than negotiation teaching and whose 200 most recent uploads are 78% under two minutes, and Recruiter Preston, whose subject is running a recruiting agency rather than negotiating as a candidate.
unprobed: negotiation academics teaching outside a business-school channel
salary-negotiation.smallRound: A --small round on job offers and counter-offers surfaced Ethan Evans, a retired Amazon vice-president — but his negotiation material is roughly twenty videos in a 459-video catalogue about promotion and executive presence, so he is listed under workplace-politics where the body of work actually is, not here.
salary-negotiation.conclusion: One creator stands. Two rounds, the second deliberately below the commercial top.
salary-negotiation.visitorNote: We searched this one twice, including a round aimed deliberately below the biggest channels. What came back was general career advice and recruiter-business content rather than anyone teaching negotiation itself at length, so one entry stands rather than a second we would not defend.

ecommerce.found: Two discovery rounds on store operations and on building and converting a store. Both returned dropshipping funnels, fulfilment vendors and agency channels: EcommOps is a third-party logistics company and its recent long-form is tariff webinars rather than teaching; Learn With Shopify is the vendor's own channel with a one-minute median; Davie Fogarty Mentors and The Ecom Academy are both course businesses whose recent long-form is AI-tooling tutorials.
unprobed: operators publishing post-mortems of their own stores
warehouse, returns and customer-service practice as its own subject
ecommerce.smallRound: The --small round, with everything above 500k subscribers hidden, changed the names and not the kind: smaller store-builder channels and coaching funnels. The pattern here is not scarcity of channels but scarcity of teaching — the subject is dominated by people selling a way to start a store.
ecommerce.conclusion: One creator stands. Two rounds, the second deliberately below the commercial top.
ecommerce.visitorNote: We searched this twice, including a round with the biggest channels hidden. Almost everything found was selling a course or a service rather than teaching the work, so one entry stands rather than a second we would not defend.

stoicism.found: Two rounds. Daily Stoic is 45 of 50 uploads under two minutes against a large commercial operation. Stoic Journal is the opposite shape and no better: 721 uploads, every one of the 50 most recent over twenty minutes, a 57-minute median, generic titles and no named teacher anywhere — a volume operation rather than a catalogue.
unprobed: classicists and philosophy departments publishing directly
stoicism.whatTheThirdRoundDid: Searched away from the commercial top — a query in the vocabulary of the primary texts (Epictetus, Seneca, commentary) with channels at 500k+ subscribers hidden. That surfaced Gregory B. Sadler's active channel: 4,071 uploads, 16 Stoic-specific videos in the last 200, Seneca read line by line and Plutarch's criticism of the Stoics given three videos of its own. Relevance ranking had been returning the same commercial incumbents whatever the phrasing.
stoicism.conclusion: RETIRED BY OUR SEARCH METHOD, NOT BY SUPPLY. The two rounds were real and both failed; the third round differed only in refusing to look at the top of the market.
